Quick Clean provides reliable residential cleaning services in Dubai for apartments, villas, and family homes. Choose a one-time clean or a recurring weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly service based on your needs.

Ideal for: Busy households & families; Working professionals; Anyone who wants a reliable recurring clean

Residential cleaning in Dubai starts at AED 200 for a Basic clean, AED 300 for Standard and AED 350 for Premium, for a studio or one bedroom apartment. Regular home cleaning is the service most of our customers use. Professional deep cleaning services in Dubai for homes that need a detailed top-to-bottom clean, including baseboards, grout, appliances, vents, and hard-to-reach areas.

Quick Clean provides professional deep cleaning services in Dubai for homes that need more than a standard clean. We tackle built-up grime, hard-to-reach areas, baseboards, grout, appliances, vents, and detailed surfaces. Deep cleaning is ideal before guests arrive, after a renovation, or as the first clean before starting a recurring service.

What's included:
- Everything in a standard clean, in greater detail
- Baseboards, door frames, and trim hand-wiped
- Inside microwave and around (behind) appliances
- Cabinet fronts and backsplash degreased
- Tile and grout scrubbed in kitchen and baths
- Vents, fans, and light fixtures dusted
- Window sills, tracks, and ledges detailed
- Buildup removed from showers and faucets

Ideal for: First-time cleans; Spring cleaning & pre-holiday; Homes that haven’t been cleaned in a while

FAQ:
- What is the difference between standard and deep cleaning in Dubai? Standard cleaning is designed to maintain an already tidy home, while deep cleaning in Dubai is more detailed and time-intensive. It targets built-up grime, baseboards, grout, vents, and areas behind or inside appliances.
- How much does deep cleaning cost in Dubai? Deep cleaning in Dubai is quoted for your property based on its size and condition. Tell us the number of bedrooms and bathrooms and whether the home is furnished, and we confirm a flat price before you book.
- How often should I schedule deep cleaning in Dubai? Most homes benefit from deep cleaning in Dubai 2–4 times a year. You may also want a deep clean before guests arrive, after renovations, or as the first visit before starting regular residential cleaning.

Quick answer: Deep cleaning is a one time, detailed clean of the whole home. It covers everything in a regular clean and adds grout, limescale, skirting boards, vents, cabinet fronts and the areas inside and around appliances. In Dubai most homes need one every three to six months. Quick Clean confirms a fixed price for your property before you book.

Dubai homes build up dirt in ways a weekly clean does not reach. Fine sand settles in window tracks, hard water leaves limescale on taps and shower glass, and air conditioning moves dust onto vents and high ledges. New homes in areas such as Dubai South, JVC and Town Square also carry building dust inside cupboards and wardrobes. A deep clean deals with all of this in one visit.

Many customers book a deep clean first and then keep the home in order with weekly or two weekly home cleaning. If you are handing a rented home back, a move out clean is the better choice because it is done in an empty home. Sofas, rugs and mattresses can be added through our carpet and upholstery cleaning. For a fuller comparison, read deep cleaning compared with regular cleaning.

More questions:
- How long does a deep clean take? Longer than a regular clean. A small apartment takes several hours, and a large apartment or a villa often takes most of a working day with a team. We give you an estimated time when we confirm the price.
- Do you bring the products and equipment for a deep clean? Yes. The team arrives with the products and equipment the job needs. If a surface such as marble or natural wood needs a product of your own, leave it out and tell us.
- Which areas do you cover for deep cleaning? We cover 27 communities across Dubai, Sharjah and Ajman, including Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, Business Bay, JVC, Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches. The same prices apply in every area and there is no travel charge.
- Do I need to prepare anything before a deep clean? Clear loose items from floors and counters so the team can reach every surface, and put valuables away. You do not need to move furniture. Tell us about heavy items you want cleaned behind.

In Dubai a tenant has to return a home in the condition it was received, apart from normal wear, and landlords often deduct cleaning costs from the deposit. ## Areas we serve
### House Cleaning Services in Dubai Marina
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/cleaning-services-dubai-marina
Part of: Dubai
Last updated: 2026-11-21

Dubai Marina is tower living from one end to the other. Buildings like Marina Gate, Cayan Tower, Princess Tower, Marina Promenade and Park Island line the water, and almost every home is an apartment. Most are studios, one bedroom and two bedroom apartments. The higher floors have three bedroom apartments, duplexes and penthouses. A lot of people here rent, and many apartments are furnished holiday homes, so people move in and out all year.

The same few things make a Marina apartment dirty. The big windows and glass balcony railings pick up salt from the sea air and a fine layer of dust, and it shows within days. Sand blows into the tracks of the sliding balcony doors. Open kitchens let cooking grease settle on the cabinet doors and the hood, and the glass shower screens get white marks from the water. None of it is hard to clean, but it needs doing often.

Quick Clean cleans apartments across Dubai Marina for residents, landlords and holiday home hosts. On every visit we clean the kitchen and bathrooms, dust the surfaces, vacuum and mop the floors, empty the bins and make the beds. A deep clean goes further. We scrub the grout, clean inside the oven and fridge, wipe the balcony glass from the inside and clear the sand out of the door tracks.

Getting into the building is the part to plan. Nearly every tower in the Marina has a reception desk, a visitor book and a separate service lift, and some ask for a pass before a cleaner can go up. Tell us the tower name and apartment number when you book, and say if your building needs a pass or a copy of an ID. We sort it out before the day so nobody is kept waiting at the desk. If you will be out, you can leave the key with the concierge.

Parking is tight in the Marina and most visitor bays are paid. That is our problem, not yours. Our cleaners usually come by metro or tram, and both stop a short walk from most towers. When we need to bring a machine for carpet or sofa cleaning, we will ask you in advance if your building has a visitor bay we can use.

Which clean you need depends on how the apartment is used. If you live there, a regular clean every week or every two weeks is usually enough, with a deep clean two or three times a year to deal with the limescale and the balcony. If you have just moved in, or the apartment has been empty over the summer, book a deep clean first. Hosts with holiday homes normally book a clean after every guest and a deep clean every couple of months, timed for a gap between bookings. If you are moving out, a move out clean covers the oven, the cupboards and the balcony, which are the things a landlord looks at before returning a deposit.

Prices are the flat rates shown in the table below, set by the size of the apartment. There is no hourly charge and no extra fee for the Marina. Same day and next day visits are often available, and early morning or evening slots work well for people on shifts and for hosts between guests. On a weekly or two weekly plan the same cleaner comes each time.

### House Cleaning Services in Downtown Dubai
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/cleaning-services-downtown-dubai
Part of: Dubai
Last updated: 2026-11-21

Downtown Dubai is a small district with a lot of homes in it. The towers along the Boulevard and around the Burj Khalifa, such as South Ridge, 29 Boulevard, Burj Vista and the Opera District buildings, are mostly studios and one bedroom apartments, with bigger apartments higher up. Old Town is different. The buildings there are low, with larger rooms, courtyards and more storage, and two and three bedroom apartments are common. Many homes in the area are serviced or let to short stay guests.

Homes here are finished to a high standard, and that changes how they should be cleaned. Marble floors and stone counters mark easily if the wrong product is used. Glossy cabinet doors scratch if they are scrubbed. There is glass everywhere, and with the building work and traffic around the Boulevard, a film of dust settles on window sills and balcony doors very quickly. Bathrooms with a lot of chrome and mirror show every water spot.

Quick Clean cleans apartments all over Downtown Dubai, in the towers and in Old Town. Each visit covers the kitchen, the bathrooms, the bedrooms and the living room, with the floors vacuumed and mopped and everything dusted. We use a gentle cleaner on marble and stone and soft cloths on glossy surfaces. A deep clean adds the grout, the inside of the oven and fridge, the cabinet fronts, the fans and the window tracks.

Access is well run but strict. Most towers have a staffed reception and a visitor register, and several want outside workers registered with the building management before they arrive. Give us the building name and apartment number when you book and tell us the rules if you know them. We do the registration ahead of the visit. For holiday homes we can work with your operator and pick up the key from the concierge.

Parking is available but paid, and the roads get busy around the mall in the evening. Our cleaners normally come by metro to the Burj Khalifa Dubai Mall station and walk from there, so parking does not hold up your booking. If we are bringing a machine for carpets or sofas, we will ask you to arrange a visitor bay for that day.

Most people who live in Downtown book a regular clean once a week or once every two weeks. Small apartments that are only used on weekdays can manage with less. A deep clean every three or four months keeps the stone, the grout and the glass looking the way they did when the apartment was new. If you let the apartment to guests, we clean after each stay so it is ready for the next arrival. Owners who are away for part of the year often ask for a clean just before they return, so the apartment is fresh and free of dust when they walk in. New homes often have a fine grey dust inside the cupboards and on top of doors and wardrobes, and a normal wipe does not get rid of it. On a windy day sand ends up on the balcony, on the window sills and across the ground floor.

For townhouses and villas, the garage and the area around the front door collect the most sand, and a quick sweep and wash there stops it from being walked through the house. ### House Cleaning Services in Expo City Dubai
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/cleaning-services-expo-city
Part of: Dubai
Last updated: 2026-10-25

Expo City Dubai is the neighbourhood that grew out of the Expo 2020 site, and it is one of the few places in Dubai where you can walk to almost everything. The homes are all apartments. Expo Village, the low rise buildings that first housed Expo staff, offers one to four bedroom apartments around shaded courtyards, while the newer Mangrove Residences, Sky Residences and Sidr Residences bring taller buildings with one to three bedroom apartments and large balconies looking over Al Wasl Plaza, Terra and the parks. Residents tend to be families and professionals who work in the district or at the airport.

The cleaning issues here are those of a brand new, very green community on the edge of the desert. Freshly handed over apartments carry construction dust in places you do not see at first, such as the tops of kitchen units, inside the wardrobes and along the balcony door tracks. The landscaping is lovely but it means pollen and fine soil on balcony floors after the irrigation runs, and the wide glass fronts that make the apartments feel bright also show every smear. Pale stone and large format tiles in most units need careful mopping with the right product rather than a quick pass. Families with young children also find that crumbs and small toys end up in the gaps of the wide plank flooring used in some of the buildings.

Quick Clean provides house cleaning across Expo City, from Expo Village to the newest towers. Discovery Gardens is a large, low rise apartment community next to Ibn Battuta Mall, built by Nakheel in themed clusters with names like Mediterranean, Zen, Contemporary, Mogul, Cactus and Mesoamerican. Almost every home here is a studio, a one bedroom or a two bedroom apartment, with a small number of larger units in the newer buildings on the edges. It is one of the most affordable places to live in new Dubai, so the residents are a mix of young professionals, couples and small families, and many share apartments. The clusters are arranged around landscaped gardens and walkways, which is pleasant but means plenty of dust and pollen find their way inside through open balcony doors.

The buildings are now fifteen years old or more, and that shows in the cleaning. Bathrooms have older grout and fittings that need regular descaling, kitchens are compact with limited ventilation so grease builds up on cabinet fronts and the extractor, and the window frames and balconies collect dust from Sheikh Zayed Road and the open land towards Al Furjan. Humidity from the air conditioning in the summer leaves a film on mirrors and glass. Pets are common, which adds hair on floors and fabric to the list.

Quick Clean provides house cleaning throughout Discovery Gardens. Because the apartments are compact, a visit is efficient, and we use the time on the places that matter most here. Discovery Gardens has its own metro station on the Route 2020 line, and Ibn Battuta station is a short walk from the eastern clusters, which is how most of our cleaners arrive for regular visits.

Jumeirah Lake Towers, which everyone in Dubai calls JLT, is a dense district of more than 80 towers arranged around three lakes, directly across Sheikh Zayed Road from Dubai Marina. The clusters are lettered A to Z, and each one holds a mix of residential and office towers such as Lake Terrace, Goldcrest Views, Saba Towers, Green Lakes, Lake Shore, Al Seef Towers, Bonnington and Dubai Gate. Homes are almost all apartments, mostly studios, one bedroom and two bedroom units, with three bedroom apartments and duplexes in the larger towers. Many residents work in the DMCC free zone towers next door.

JLT apartments share the cleaning issues of any busy tower district, with a few of their own. Floor to ceiling glass facing the lakes shows every smear and picks up dust from the constant traffic on Sheikh Zayed Road and First Al Khail Street. Open kitchens send cooking residue onto nearby surfaces. The older towers from the first phase have bathrooms with grout and glass screens that need regular descaling. Many apartments are rented furnished or used as short stay lets, so turnovers between tenants and guests are frequent. Pets are allowed in many towers, so hair on sofas and rugs comes up often, and the balconies above the lakes collect a surprising amount of dust.

Quick Clean provides house cleaning across every JLT cluster. Each visit covers the kitchen, bathrooms, bedrooms and living space, with floors vacuumed and mopped, interior glass and mirrors polished and the balcony door tracks wiped out. Access in JLT runs through the tower receptions. Visitor bays are few and usually paid, and the cluster roads are one way loops that get congested, so our cleaners arrive by metro for regular visits. Palm Jumeirah is unlike anywhere else we clean. Sea air is the defining cleaning problem on the Palm. Salt settles on glass, balcony railings, outdoor furniture and pool decks within days, leaving a haze that ordinary wiping only spreads around. In the apartments, the large glass fronts and the balconies take the most work, and furnished holiday homes need everything from the linen to the inside of the fridge checked between guests.

Outdoor kitchens and barbecue areas on the fronds get a proper degrease rather than a wipe, and pool furniture cushions are brushed down and wiped.

Access on the Palm is controlled. ## Guides
### How Much Does House Cleaning Cost in Dubai
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/guides/house-cleaning-cost-dubai
Last updated: 2026-11-20

Short answer: House cleaning in Dubai is sold in two ways, by the hour or as a flat rate for the home. Quick Clean charges a flat rate by unit type. A studio or one bedroom apartment costs AED 200 on the Basic plan, AED 300 on Standard and AED 350 on Premium, and a six bedroom villa costs AED 800 to AED 1050.

#### The two ways cleaning is priced in Dubai

Most cleaning in Dubai is sold by the hour. You choose how many cleaners and how many hours, and you pay for the time whether or not the home is finished. It looks cheap on the booking screen, but the final cost depends on how fast the cleaner works and how well you guessed the hours. If the visit runs short, the last rooms get rushed or skipped.

The other way is a flat rate for the home. The company prices the job by the type and size of the property, and the price does not change if the work takes longer than planned. This is how Quick Clean prices every regular clean. You see the full amount before you book and the cleaner stays until the checklist is done.

#### Quick Clean prices for apartments

Apartment prices rise with the number of bedrooms. These are the published rates per visit.

- Studio or one bedroom apartment. Basic AED 200, Standard AED 300, Premium AED 350.
- Two bedroom apartment. Basic AED 300, Standard AED 400, Premium AED 450.
- Three bedroom apartment. Basic AED 400, Standard AED 500, Premium AED 550.
- Four bedroom apartment or penthouse. Basic AED 450, Standard AED 600, Premium AED 700.

#### Quick Clean prices for villas

Villas cost more than apartments with the same number of bedrooms because they have more floors, more bathrooms and more floor area to cover.

- Three bedroom villa. Basic AED 500, Standard AED 650, Premium AED 750.
- Four bedroom villa. Basic AED 600, Standard AED 750, Premium AED 850.
- Five bedroom villa. Basic AED 700, Standard AED 850, Premium AED 950.
- Six bedroom villa. Basic AED 800, Standard AED 950, Premium AED 1050.

#### What the three plans include

The plans differ in who provides the linens and the supplies, not in how carefully the home is cleaned.

- Basic covers cleaning, housekeeping and laundry. You provide the linens and the cleaning supplies.
- Standard covers cleaning and laundry, and we bring the cleaning supplies. You provide the linens.
- Premium is the full service. We provide the cleaning, the linens and laundry, the supplies and the guest amenities.

#### What changes the price of a clean

Four things decide what a clean costs anywhere in Dubai. The first is the size and type of the home. The second is the kind of clean, because a deep clean or a move out clean takes far longer than a regular visit. The third is who supplies the products and equipment. The fourth is how often you book, since recurring visits are quicker for the cleaner than a first visit to a home that has not been cleaned for a while.

Add on work is priced separately. With Quick Clean, carpet and upholstery cleaning starts at AED 89 and window and glass cleaning starts at AED 69. Deep cleaning and move in or move out cleaning are quoted for your property before you book, because the condition of the home matters more than its size.

#### How to compare two quotes fairly

Ask each company the same five questions. Is the price fixed or by the hour? Are supplies and equipment included? How many cleaners will come and for how long? What happens if you are not happy with part of the clean? Is there a travel charge for your area? A low hourly rate with no supplies, one cleaner and no guarantee often costs more than a flat rate once the visit is over.

FAQ:
- What is the cheapest house cleaning price with Quick Clean? The lowest plan price is AED 200 for a Basic clean of a studio or one bedroom apartment. Standard for the same home is AED 300 and Premium is AED 350.
- How much does it cost to clean a two bedroom apartment in Dubai? With Quick Clean a two bedroom apartment costs AED 300 on Basic, AED 400 on Standard and AED 450 on Premium, per visit, as a flat rate.
- Is there a travel charge for my area? No. The same flat rates apply in every community we serve across Dubai, Sharjah and Ajman.
- Why is deep cleaning not on the price list? A deep clean depends on the condition of the home as much as its size, so we confirm a flat price for your property before you book rather than publish a figure that may not fit.

### Deep Cleaning vs Regular Cleaning and Which One You Need
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/guides/deep-cleaning-vs-regular-cleaning
Last updated: 2026-11-20

Short answer: A regular clean maintains a home that is already in good order. It covers surfaces, floors, the kitchen and the bathrooms. A deep clean resets a home. It adds the slow detailed work a regular visit has no time for, such as grout, skirting boards, vents, door frames and the areas inside and behind appliances. Most homes need one deep clean first and regular cleans after that.

#### What a regular clean covers

A regular clean keeps a home at the standard it already has. It is built around the things that get dirty every week.

- Kitchen counters, sink, hob and the outside of appliances wiped down.
- Bathrooms cleaned, including the toilet, shower, bath, basin and mirror.
- All reachable surfaces and fixtures dusted.
- Carpets and rugs vacuumed and hard floors mopped.
- Beds made and living areas tidied.
- Bins emptied and liners replaced.
- Switches, handles and other high touch points wiped.

#### What a deep clean adds

A deep clean includes everything above and then goes after the build up that a weekly visit never reaches.

- Skirting boards, door frames and trim wiped by hand.
- Tile and grout scrubbed in the kitchen and bathrooms.
- Limescale and soap build up removed from showers and taps.
- Cabinet fronts and splashbacks degreased.
- The inside of the microwave and the areas around and behind appliances.
- Vents, fans and light fittings dusted.
- Window sills, tracks and ledges cleaned out.

#### How long each one takes

A regular clean usually takes between one and a half and three hours, depending on the size and condition of the home. A deep clean takes noticeably longer, often most of a working day for a large apartment or a villa, and it is usually done by a team rather than one person. That extra time is the reason the two are priced differently.

#### Signs your home needs a deep clean

You do not need a deep clean every month. You need one when a regular clean no longer makes the home look clean.

- The grout between tiles has turned grey or brown.
- Taps and shower glass have a white crust that wiping does not move.
- There is a sticky film on kitchen cabinet doors near the hob.
- Dust has gathered on air conditioning vents and the tops of doors.
- The home has not been professionally cleaned for three months or more.
- You have just taken the keys to a new home or finished a renovation.
- Guests are coming to stay or a new baby is on the way.

#### Why Dubai homes need deep cleans more often

Three things about Dubai speed up the build up. Fine sand gets in through window tracks and balcony doors even when they are closed. The water is hard enough in many buildings to leave limescale on taps and glass within weeks. Air conditioning runs for most of the year and moves dust around the home, so vents and the tops of furniture collect it quickly. A home that would manage on one deep clean a year elsewhere often needs two or three here.

#### The pattern that works for most homes

Start with one deep clean. Follow it with a regular clean every week or every two weeks. Book another deep clean every three to six months, or after the summer when the dust and humidity have done their work. Starting a recurring plan without a deep clean first means the cleaner spends every visit catching up rather than maintaining.

With Quick Clean, regular cleans are a flat rate by unit type from AED 200. Deep cleans are quoted for your property before you book.

FAQ:
- Can I book a regular clean for a home that really needs a deep clean? You can, but the result will disappoint. A regular visit does not include the time for grout, limescale and built up grease, so the home will look tidy rather than clean. One deep clean first makes every later visit worth more.
- How often should I book a deep clean in Dubai? Every three to six months suits most homes. Homes with pets, young children or a lot of cooking are better at every three months, and homes cleaned weekly can stretch to six.
- Is a move out clean the same as a deep clean? It is a deep clean of an empty home with extra attention to the things a landlord checks, such as the inside of cupboards, the oven, the balcony and marks on the walls.
- Do I need to move furniture before a deep clean? No. The cleaners move light furniture themselves. Tell us in advance about heavy items you want cleaned behind so the team plans for it.

### Move Out Cleaning Checklist for Dubai Tenants
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/guides/move-out-cleaning-checklist-dubai
Last updated: 2026-11-20

Short answer: Under Dubai tenancy law a tenant must hand the property back in the condition it was received, apart from ordinary wear and tear. In practice that means an empty, fully cleaned home with the oven, cupboards, bathrooms, balcony and floors all done. Cleaning is one of the most common reasons landlords deduct from the security deposit, so it is worth doing properly and keeping photos.

#### What the law and your landlord expect

Article 21 of Dubai Law 26 of 2007 says the tenant must return the property in the same condition it was in when the lease began, except for ordinary wear and tear. Faded paint and light marks from furniture are wear and tear. Grease in the oven, limescale in the shower and a dusty balcony are not.

The security deposit in Dubai is usually 5 percent of the annual rent for an unfurnished home and 10 percent for a furnished one. The landlord can deduct the cost of cleaning and repairs from it. If you disagree with a deduction, the Rental Dispute Centre is the body that hears the case, and photos taken on handover day are the best evidence you can bring.

#### Kitchen checklist

The kitchen is where most deductions start, so give it the most time.

- Oven, grill and hob degreased inside and out, including the trays and racks.
- Extractor hood and its filter cleaned.
- Fridge and freezer emptied, defrosted, wiped inside and left with the doors open.
- Every cupboard and drawer emptied and wiped inside.
- Sink, taps and drain descaled.
- Splashback and worktops cleaned of grease and stains.
- Washing machine drawer and door seal wiped.

#### Bathroom checklist

Bathrooms are judged on limescale and grout.

- Shower glass, taps and shower heads descaled.
- Tile grout scrubbed and any mould removed.
- Toilet cleaned inside, outside and behind.
- Basin, vanity unit and mirror cleaned, with cupboards emptied.
- Extractor fan cover dusted.
- Floor drains cleared of hair.

#### Bedrooms and living areas checklist

With the furniture gone, everything that was hidden is on show.

- Wardrobes emptied and wiped inside, including the top shelves.
- Skirting boards, door frames and doors wiped.
- Light switches and sockets wiped.
- Air conditioning vents dusted.
- Windows cleaned inside and the tracks cleared of sand.
- Floors vacuumed and mopped, including the corners where furniture stood.
- Scuffs and marks on walls gently cleaned where the paint allows.

#### Balcony, storage and outside areas

These are the areas tenants forget and landlords always open.

- Balcony floor swept and washed, railings and glass wiped.
- Storage room and utility cupboard emptied and swept.
- For villas, the garage floor swept and the patio washed down.
- All rubbish removed from the property, not left by the door.

#### The order to do things in

Timing matters as much as effort. Follow this order and the clean only has to be done once.

- Tell your landlord or agent your handover date in writing.
- Book the movers and get a move out permit from the building management if your building requires one.
- Do repairs first, such as filling nail holes and replacing dead bulbs.
- Clean after the movers have left, so the home is empty.
- Take dated photos and a video of every room once the clean is finished.
- Keep the electricity and water connected until the handover inspection is over, then request your final bill.

#### Doing it yourself or hiring a team

A move out clean of an empty two bedroom apartment takes two people most of a day if the oven and bathrooms need real work. If you are packing, working and arranging movers in the same week, a professional team is usually the safer choice. Quick Clean quotes move out cleans for your property before you book, and if the inspection finds an area that is not right, tell us within 24 hours and we come back and clean it again at no charge.

FAQ:
- Can my landlord deduct cleaning costs from my deposit in Dubai? Yes, if the home is not returned in the condition it was received. The landlord cannot charge for ordinary wear and tear, and you can take a disputed deduction to the Rental Dispute Centre.
- Should I clean before or after the movers come? After. An empty home lets the cleaners reach the floors, skirting boards and the inside of every wardrobe and cupboard, which is exactly what the inspection looks at.
- Does a move out clean include painting? No. Cleaning and painting are separate jobs. Check your tenancy contract, because some contracts ask the tenant to repaint and some do not.
- How far ahead should I book a move out clean? A few days ahead is best, and at least one day before the handover inspection so there is time to fix anything that is missed.

### How Often Should You Clean Your Home in Dubai
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/guides/how-often-to-clean-your-home-in-dubai
Last updated: 2026-11-20

Short answer: Most homes in Dubai do best with a professional clean every one or two weeks and a deep clean every three to six months. Households with children or pets usually need weekly visits. A single person or a couple in a small apartment can manage on a visit every two weeks. Dust and limescale build up faster here than in cooler, wetter climates, so monthly visits are rarely enough on their own.

#### Why Dubai homes get dirty faster

Fine desert sand is always in the air and it finds its way in through window tracks, balcony doors and the air conditioning. Humidity is high through the summer months, which encourages mould in bathrooms and around window seals. The water leaves limescale on taps, shower glass and kettles. None of this is a sign of a badly kept home. It simply means the schedule that worked in another country will fall short here.

#### How often to book a cleaner by household

Use the number of people and how the home is used as your guide.

- Family with children. Weekly.
- Home with a dog or a cat. Weekly, with extra attention to floors and sofas.
- Couple or two sharers who both work. Every two weeks.
- One person in a studio or one bedroom apartment. Every two weeks.
- Home that is empty for much of the year. Once a month, plus a clean before each stay.
- Villa with a garden and outdoor seating. Weekly inside, with patios and outdoor glass every two to four weeks.

#### Jobs to do every day or two

These take minutes and stop the weekly clean from turning into a rescue.

- Wipe kitchen counters and the hob after cooking.
- Wash up or run the dishwasher.
- Squeegee the shower glass after use to slow limescale.
- Take out food waste, which attracts insects quickly in the heat.

#### Jobs to do every week

This is what a regular professional clean covers.

- Vacuum and mop all floors.
- Clean bathrooms fully.
- Dust surfaces, shelves and electronics.
- Change bed linen.
- Wipe handles, switches and remote controls.
- Sweep the balcony.

#### Jobs to do every month

These are easy to forget because the dirt is out of sight.

- Wipe air conditioning vents and clean or rinse the filters.
- Clear sand from window and balcony door tracks.
- Clean inside the microwave and wipe the fridge shelves.
- Descale the kettle and the shower head.
- Wash the balcony floor and wipe the railings.

#### Jobs to do every three to six months

This is the deep clean list.

- Scrub tile grout in the kitchen and bathrooms.
- Degrease cabinet fronts and the extractor hood.
- Clean behind and under the fridge, cooker and washing machine.
- Have carpets, rugs and sofas professionally cleaned.
- Wash curtains or have blinds dusted and wiped.
- Clean windows inside and out where they can be reached safely.

#### Adjusting for the seasons

Summer is the hard season. Windows stay shut, the air conditioning runs all day and humidity rises, so bathrooms and vents need more attention and a deep clean at the end of summer is well timed. From late winter into spring the shamal winds bring dust storms, and balconies and window tracks need clearing after each one. Before long holidays, when many residents travel, a clean on the day you leave means you do not come home to stale air and dust.

Recurring plans with Quick Clean start at AED 200 per visit for a studio or one bedroom apartment, and on a recurring plan the same cleaner comes each time.

FAQ:
- Is a monthly clean enough for an apartment in Dubai? Only for a home that is lightly used. For a home that is lived in every day, dust and limescale build up too far in four weeks, and each visit becomes a deep clean rather than a regular one.
- How often should air conditioning vents be cleaned? Wipe the vents and rinse the filters about once a month. The ducts and the unit itself should be serviced by an air conditioning company, usually once or twice a year.
- How often should carpets and sofas be cleaned? Every six months suits most homes, and every three to four months if you have pets, young children or allergies.
- Does weekly cleaning cost more per visit than cleaning every two weeks? The published flat rate is per visit by unit type, and recurring customers can save up to 20 percent on each clean after the first.

### Holiday Home Turnover Cleaning Checklist for Dubai Hosts
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/guides/holiday-home-turnover-cleaning-dubai
Last updated: 2026-11-20

Short answer: A turnover clean prepares a holiday home for the next guest between check out and check in. It covers a full clean, fresh linens and towels, restocked supplies and a check for damage or missing items. In Dubai the window is usually only four or five hours. Quick Clean prices turnovers as a flat rate by unit type, from AED 200 to AED 350 for a studio or one bedroom apartment depending on who provides the linens and supplies.

#### How a turnover differs from a normal clean

A normal clean is for the person who lives in the home. A turnover is for a stranger who has seen photos and paid for a hotel standard. That changes the job. Hair in a drain or a mark on a pillowcase that a resident would ignore becomes a bad review. A turnover also includes tasks that are not cleaning at all, such as counting towels, checking the remote controls work and reporting a broken glass.

Holiday homes in Dubai are licensed by the Department of Economy and Tourism, and guests can complain to the platform or the authority about cleanliness. A reliable turnover routine protects both your rating and your permit.

#### Turnover checklist for every room

Work through the home in the same order every time so nothing is missed.

- Strip all beds and remake them with fresh linen, checking the mattress protector for stains.
- Replace bath towels, hand towels and bath mats.
- Clean bathrooms fully and clear every drain of hair.
- Clean the kitchen, including inside the microwave, the fridge and the oven if it was used.
- Wash, dry and put away all dishes, and empty the dishwasher.
- Dust surfaces, wipe mirrors and glass, and remove fingerprints from switches and handles.
- Vacuum and mop all floors, including under the beds and the sofa.
- Sweep the balcony and wipe the outdoor furniture.
- Empty every bin and take the rubbish out of the unit.

#### Restocking and checks

These are the items guests notice within the first ten minutes.

- Toilet paper, hand soap, shampoo and shower gel.
- Dishwashing liquid, a clean sponge and bin liners.
- Drinking water, tea and coffee if you provide them.
- Air conditioning set to a comfortable temperature before arrival.
- Lights, television, remote controls and the internet connection tested.
- Lost property collected and reported to the host.
- Damage, stains and missing items photographed and reported the same day.

#### Timing between guests

Most Dubai listings use a late morning check out and a mid afternoon check in, which leaves four to five hours. A studio or one bedroom apartment can be turned over well inside that. A three bedroom apartment or a villa needs a team rather than one cleaner. Laundry is the bottleneck. A second and third set of linen for every bed means the cleaner can remake the beds straight away and the washing can follow, and it is the single change that makes same day turnovers reliable.

#### What a turnover costs with Quick Clean

The three plans suit the way hosts work. The price is per turnover and depends on the unit type and on who provides the linens and supplies.

- Basic, from AED 200. Cleaning, housekeeping and laundry, with linens and supplies provided by the owner.
- Standard, from AED 300. Cleaning and laundry with our cleaning supplies, and linens provided by the owner.
- Premium, from AED 350. The full service, with linens, laundry, supplies and guest amenities provided by us.
- A two bedroom apartment costs AED 300, AED 400 or AED 450 on the three plans.
- A four bedroom villa costs AED 600, AED 750 or AED 850 on the three plans.

#### Keeping standards up between deep cleans

Turnovers keep a unit presentable but they do not stop slow build up. Plan a deep clean every two to three months for a busy listing, with grout, limescale, the oven, the vents and the sofa all done, and schedule it for a gap between bookings. Have carpets and upholstery cleaned at the same time. Hosts who do this find that each turnover is quicker and that cleanliness scores stay steady through the high season.

FAQ:
- How long does a turnover clean take? It depends on the size of the unit and how the guests left it. A studio or one bedroom apartment fits comfortably between a late morning check out and an afternoon check in, and larger units are handled by a team so they fit the same window.
- Can you provide the linens and guest amenities? Yes. On the Premium plan we provide linens, laundry, cleaning supplies and guest amenities. On Standard we bring the supplies and you provide the linens, and on Basic you provide both.
- Do you report damage or missing items? Ask for it when you book. The cleaner can photograph anything broken, stained or missing and send it to you on the day, so you can raise it with the guest or the platform in time.
- Can I book turnovers at short notice? Same day and next day slots are often available. For a busy listing, tell us your bookings as they come in so each turnover is scheduled early.

### Hourly Maid Service or Flat Rate Cleaning in Dubai
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/guides/hourly-maid-vs-flat-rate-cleaning-dubai
Last updated: 2026-11-20

Short answer: Hourly maid service charges for time, so you pay for the hours booked whether or not the home is finished. Flat rate cleaning charges for the result, so the price is fixed for your home and the cleaner stays until the checklist is done. Hourly suits small top up jobs where you direct the work. Flat rate suits full home cleans where you want a known price and a known outcome.

#### How hourly maid service works

You book a number of cleaners for a number of hours, usually with a minimum of two hours. Cleaning materials are often an extra charge per hour. The cleaner arrives, you tell them what to do, and they stop when the time is up. The advertised hourly rate is low, which is why this is the most common way to book a cleaner in Dubai.

The weakness is that all the risk sits with you. If you guess too few hours, the last rooms are rushed or left. If you guess too many, you pay for time you did not need. The total also grows once materials, a second cleaner and any minimum booking are added.

#### How flat rate cleaning works

The company prices the job by the type and size of the home and commits to a checklist. You know the total before you book. If the work takes longer than planned, that is the company's problem rather than yours. Quick Clean works this way. A two bedroom apartment is AED 300, AED 400 or AED 450 per visit depending on the plan, and that figure does not move on the day.

#### Side by side

The differences that matter in practice.

- Price certainty. Hourly depends on how long the job takes. Flat rate is fixed before you book.
- Who plans the work. With hourly, you direct the cleaner. With flat rate, the cleaner follows a set checklist.
- If the job runs over. With hourly you pay more or accept less. With flat rate the cleaner finishes at no extra cost.
- Supplies. Often an extra charge with hourly bookings. With flat rate it depends on the plan and is stated up front.
- Quality guarantee. Rare with hourly bookings, since you bought time. Quick Clean will clean any area again at no charge if you tell us within 24 hours.
- Best for. Hourly suits ironing, a quick tidy or one room. Flat rate suits a full home clean.

#### When hourly is the better choice

Hourly service makes sense when the job is small and you know exactly what you want done. Two hours of ironing, a kitchen tidy after a dinner, or help with one room before guests arrive are all good examples. It also suits people who are at home and like to direct the work themselves.

#### When flat rate is the better choice

Flat rate is the better choice for a full clean of the home, for recurring weekly or two weekly visits, for villas where it is hard to guess the hours, and for anyone who will not be at home during the clean. It is also the safer choice for holiday homes, where the unit has to be guest ready by a fixed time and nobody is there to supervise.

#### Questions to ask before you book either

Whichever you choose, get clear answers to these.

- What is the total I will pay, including materials and any fees?
- Is there a minimum number of hours or a travel charge?
- Are the cleaners employed by the company and insured?
- Will the same cleaner come each time?
- What happens if I am not happy with the result?

FAQ:
- Is flat rate cleaning more expensive than hourly? Not necessarily. Once materials, a minimum booking and a second cleaner are added, an hourly booking for a full home often costs the same or more, without a fixed result.
- What if my home is much dirtier than average? Tell us when you book. A home that has not been cleaned for a long time may need a deep clean first, which is quoted for your property, and regular flat rate visits after that.
- Can I add extra tasks to a flat rate clean? Yes. Carpet and upholstery cleaning starts at AED 89 and window and glass cleaning starts at AED 69, and both can be added to a visit.
- Do I need to be home for a flat rate clean? No. Most customers leave access instructions and come home to a clean house. You are welcome to be there if you prefer.

### How to Prepare Your Home for a Professional Cleaner
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/guides/how-to-prepare-for-a-cleaning-visit
Last updated: 2026-11-20

Short answer: You do not need to clean before the cleaner comes. You only need to clear the way. Pick up clothes, toys and loose items so surfaces and floors can be reached, put away valuables and documents, arrange building access and tell the cleaner about anything fragile or anything you want done first. Ten minutes of preparation means the visit is spent cleaning rather than tidying.

#### Tidy, do not clean

A cleaner cannot wipe a counter that is covered in post or vacuum a floor covered in toys. Every minute spent moving things is a minute not spent cleaning. Before the visit, do a quick pass through each room.

- Pick clothes up off floors, beds and chairs.
- Put toys in their boxes.
- Clear kitchen counters of dishes and food.
- Stack loose papers in one place and say whether they should be left alone.
- Clear the floor of the shower and the edge of the bath.

#### Put away what matters

Reputable cleaners are vetted and insured, and problems are rare. It is still sensible to put cash, jewellery, passports and important documents in a drawer or a safe. It removes any chance of something being moved and mislaid, and it lets the cleaner work without worrying about delicate personal items.

#### Arrange access in advance

Access is the most common reason a clean starts late in Dubai. Sort it out when you book rather than on the day.

- Tell building security or reception that a cleaner is expected, and register them as a visitor if your tower requires it.
- Share the gate code or community pass details for gated villa communities.
- Say where visitors can park, especially if the cleaner is bringing carpet or upholstery equipment.
- If you will be out, leave the key or access card with reception, or share the door code.
- Give a phone number that will be answered if the cleaner is held at the gate.

#### Tell the cleaner what you want

A two minute message saves a lot of guessing. Say which rooms matter most, which surfaces need special care such as marble, natural wood or a delicate hob, and whether there are rooms to skip. If you have a product you prefer for a particular surface, leave it out on the counter. If someone in the home has allergies or asthma, mention that too.

#### Pets and children

Let the cleaner know about pets before the visit. Keep dogs in one room or take them out for a walk during the clean, both for the comfort of the pet and so that doors can be opened freely. Cats usually hide and are fine. With small children at home, plan for one room at a time to be out of bounds while the floor dries.

#### On the day and afterwards

If you are home, walk the cleaner through the house at the start and then leave them to work. At the end, look at the kitchen, the bathrooms and the floors, which are the places where the difference shows. If something is not right, say so straight away or within 24 hours. With Quick Clean, any area you are not happy with is cleaned again at no charge.

On a recurring plan the same cleaner returns each time, so the briefing gets shorter with every visit. After two or three cleans most customers stop preparing at all beyond picking things up off the floor.

FAQ:
- Should I clean before the cleaner arrives? No. Tidy loose items away so surfaces and floors are clear, and leave the actual cleaning to the cleaner. That is what you are paying for.
- Do I need to provide cleaning products? It depends on the plan. On Standard and Premium we bring the cleaning supplies. On Basic the owner provides them. If you have a product you prefer, leave it out and tell us.
- Do I need to be home during the clean? No. Most customers give secure access instructions and come home to a clean house. You are welcome to stay if you prefer.
- Should I tip my cleaner in Dubai? Tipping is not required. It is a personal choice, and some customers tip after a particularly good clean or on a recurring plan around holidays.

### How to Clean Your Home After a Sandstorm in Dubai
URL: https://www.quickclean.ae/guides/cleaning-after-a-sandstorm-dubai
Last updated: 2026-11-20

Short answer: After a sandstorm, wait until the dust has settled, then work from the outside in and from the top down. Start with the balcony and the window tracks, rinse the air conditioning filters, dust high surfaces with a damp cloth, then vacuum and mop the floors last. Use damp cloths and a vacuum rather than a dry duster or a broom, which only lift the fine dust back into the air.

#### Before the storm arrives

A few minutes of preparation halves the cleaning afterwards. Close all windows and balcony doors and check that they are latched. Bring cushions, rugs and laundry in from the balcony. Lay a rolled towel along the bottom of balcony doors and any window that does not seal well. If your air conditioning has a fresh air setting, switch it to recirculate until the storm has passed.

#### Wait for the dust to settle

Fine dust stays in the air for hours after the wind drops. If you clean too early it simply settles again on the surfaces you have just wiped. Wait until the air outside looks clear, which is often the next morning, before you start on the balcony and the windows.

#### Step by step, from the outside in

Follow this order so you are never cleaning the same surface twice.

- Sweep the balcony gently, then wash the floor with water and wipe the railings and furniture.
- Vacuum the sand out of window and balcony door tracks, then wipe them with a damp cloth.
- Wipe the window sills and the inside of the glass.
- Remove the air conditioning filters, rinse them under running water, let them dry fully and refit them.
- Wipe the air conditioning vents and the tops of doors, wardrobes and shelves with a damp cloth.
- Dust tables, counters, electronics and other surfaces, rinsing the cloth often.
- Vacuum sofas, cushions, curtains and mattresses.
- Vacuum all floors, including under the furniture, then mop hard floors with clean water changed often.

#### Mistakes that make it worse

Sand is abrasive and the fine dust is very light, so some habits do real harm.

- Using a dry duster or a feather duster, which throws the dust back into the air.
- Sweeping indoor floors with a broom instead of vacuuming.
- Wiping glass, screens or polished surfaces with a dry cloth, which can scratch them.
- Mopping before vacuuming, which turns the dust into mud in the grout lines.
- Forgetting the air conditioning filters, so the unit blows dust around for weeks.

#### Carpets, sofas and curtains

Soft furnishings hold more dust than any hard surface. Vacuum them slowly, going over each area more than once. If people in the home are sneezing or the room smells dusty a few days later, the dust is in the fabric, and a professional carpet and upholstery clean is the fix. With Quick Clean that service starts at AED 89.

#### Villas and ground floor homes

Homes at ground level take in far more sand than apartments on high floors. After a storm, hose down the patio and the paths before anyone walks the sand inside, clear the tracks of every sliding door, and sweep the garage. Outdoor glass and window frames can be rinsed with water first and then wiped, never wiped dry. Check the outdoor air conditioning units for a layer of sand on the fins, and have them serviced if the cooling drops.

#### When to call in a cleaner

If the storm was heavy, if a window or balcony door was left open, or if someone in the home has asthma or allergies, a professional clean is worth it. Ask for a deep clean rather than a regular visit if dust has reached inside cupboards and wardrobes. Storms are most common from late winter through spring and again in summer, so many households time a deep clean for the end of the dusty season.

FAQ:
- How soon after a sandstorm should I clean? Wait until the dust has settled and the air outside is clear, usually the next morning. Cleaning during the storm or straight after it means the dust settles again on clean surfaces.
- How do I get sand out of window tracks? Vacuum the loose sand first with a narrow nozzle, loosen what is left with a small dry brush, vacuum again and finish with a damp cloth.
- Should I clean my air conditioning after a sandstorm? Yes. Rinse and dry the filters and wipe the vents after any heavy storm. If the air still smells dusty or the cooling is weaker, book a service with an air conditioning company.
- Is a regular clean enough after a sandstorm? After a light storm with the windows shut, yes. After a heavy storm, or if a door or window was open, a deep clean is the better choice because dust will have reached inside cupboards, tracks and soft furnishings.

## General FAQ
- Do I need to be home during the clean? No. Most customers give us secure access instructions and come home to a spotless space. You are welcome to be there if you prefer.
- What if I am not happy with the clean? Just let us know within 24 hours and we will send someone back to re-clean the area free. That is our 100% Spotless Guarantee.
- Are your cleaners insured and background-checked? Yes. Every Quick Clean pro is interviewed, background-checked, trained, and fully insured and bonded before they ever enter a home.
- Do you bring your own supplies? Yes. We arrive with professional, eco-friendly products and equipment. Have a preferred product? Just leave it out and let us know.
- How do I pay, and when? Securely online after the clean is done and you are happy. No cash needed, no payment up front, and no contracts.
- How much does house cleaning cost with Quick Clean? Every plan is a flat rate by unit type. Basic starts at AED 200 for a studio or one bedroom apartment, Standard at AED 300 and Premium at AED 350, and the pricing page lists every unit type from a studio up to a six bedroom villa. Deep cleans and move in or move out cleans are quoted for your property before you book.
- Which areas do you serve? Quick Clean serves Dubai, Sharjah, and Ajman — including Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, JVC, Business Bay, and surrounding communities.
- How long does a house cleaning take? A standard clean usually takes about 1.5 to 3 hours, depending on the size and condition of your home. Deep cleans and move-in/move-out cleans take longer. You will get an estimated time when you book.
- Can I book a same-day or next-day cleaning? Yes. Same-day and next-day appointments are often available. You can book online in about 60 seconds and choose the earliest time slot that works for you.
- What types of properties do you clean? We clean apartments, villas, townhouses, and studios, as well as offices and commercial spaces. The same 100% Spotless Guarantee applies to every property type and size.
- What is included in a standard cleaning? A standard clean covers your kitchen, bathrooms, bedrooms, and living areas — dusting, vacuuming, mopping, wiping surfaces and counters, emptying bins, and tidying. Extras like inside the oven or baseboards can be added as a deep clean.
- What is the difference between a standard clean and a deep clean? A standard clean maintains an already-tidy home. A deep clean is more thorough and adds baseboards, grout, vents, and inside or behind appliances. Many customers start with a deep clean, then switch to recurring standard cleans.
- How often should I schedule a cleaning? Most households choose bi-weekly cleaning. Homes with kids or pets often prefer weekly, while lighter homes do well with monthly visits. Recurring plans save up to 20% per visit.
- Are your cleaning products safe for children and pets? Yes. We use professional, eco-friendly, non-toxic products that are safe around children and pets. If you prefer specific products, just leave them out and let us know.
- Can I request the same cleaner every time? Yes. On recurring plans we send the same vetted cleaner who already knows your home and your preferences.
- What payment methods do you accept? You pay securely online by credit or debit card after the clean is finished and you are happy with it. No cash is needed and no payment is taken up front.
- Can I reschedule or cancel my cleaning? Yes. You can reschedule or cancel anytime from your booking confirmation. There are no contracts and no cancellation fees — we just appreciate a little notice when possible.
- What happens if something is damaged during the clean? Quick Clean is fully insured and bonded. In the rare event something is damaged, let us know within 24 hours and we will make it right.
- Do you offer office or commercial cleaning? Yes. We provide after-hours office and commercial cleaning on a custom recurring schedule. Request a free walkthrough and we will send you a flat quote.
